summary: Stereo imager for masters and buses: four bands (zero-latency Linkwitz–Riley crossovers) with the width of each from 0 to 200 % (the side against the mid, in the band), a Stereoize amount per band that adds a decorrelated copy of the mid to the side (the mono sum is untouched, so it is safe in mono), and Recover sides, which returns the side that narrowing took away to the mid through a 90 degree allpass pair so it does not comb in mono. Per-band width and correlation readings, Delta (hear only what it changes) and a gain-match reading. Use it to widen the highs, narrow and focus the lows, or fix a mix that collapses in mono.

parameters.name: Crossover 1
parameters.description: Between the first and the second band

parameters.name: Crossover 2
parameters.description: Between the second and the third band (never below Crossover 1)

parameters.name: Crossover 3
parameters.description: Between the third and the fourth band (never below Crossover 2)

parameters.name: Width 1
parameters.description: The first band's width: the side against the mid. 0 % is mono, 100 % as it came in, 200 % twice the side

parameters.name: Stereoize 1
parameters.description: Adds a decorrelated copy of the first band's mid to its side (the mono sum is not changed). 0 % off

parameters.name: Recover sides
parameters.description: The side that narrowing takes away is returned to the mid, turned 90 degrees against it so it adds to the level without combing

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the imager, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what the imager changes: the output minus the input (glides over 10 ms)

readings.description: Side against mid in the first band, dB of energy, at the output (−100 when there is no side)
The second band's side against mid
The third band's side against mid
The fourth band's side against mid
Correlation of left and right in the first band at the output, −1 … +1
Short-term loudness out − in (K-weighted, 3 s): what Output would have to take back for equal loudness
Always 0: the imager adds no latency
